title: Learn Enough to Invest Smart
quote: Do not spend months researching. Learn enough to move.
description: Before you invest a single dollar, you need to understand the landscape. This phase covers machine types, real costs, and what locations actually care about — so you can make smart decisions from day one.

tasks.text: Research machine types: snack/drink combos, smart coolers, micro markets, and specialty machines.
Understand costs: used vs. new equipment, financing vs. cash, and ongoing service fees.
Learn ROI thinking — project your returns before you invest a single dollar.
Research location commissions — what to expect and how to negotiate.
Understand what locations actually care about: reliability, cleanliness, and zero hassle.

tips: Snaxology specializes in premium micro markets and AI-powered smart coolers — zero cost to the location, fully managed service, and timely restocking every time.
Smart coolers use AI-powered grab-and-go technology. Micro markets are open-concept self-service stores ideal for high-traffic venues.
Locations want professional operators they can trust long-term — not hobbyists testing the waters.

title: Build Your Foundation
quote: Your credibility begins here, before you ever walk through a door.
description: These five days of setup work will save you weeks of rejection. Completing these steps before your first outreach call signals to location owners that you are a serious, professional operator — not a hobbyist testing the waters.

tasks.text: Choose a business name that reflects your brand.
Check LLC availability in your state and register your business (LLC or Sole Prop).
Apply for an EIN through the IRS (free at irs.gov).
Set up a dedicated business phone number.
Create a professional business email address.
Open a dedicated business bank account.

tips: Snaxology partners operate under a proven brand with marketing support, professional materials, and a track record that opens doors faster than any solo operator can build alone.
A registered business with a professional email and phone number immediately separates you from the competition and earns you a real conversation.
Operators who skip this step spend months pitching and losing deals they should have won.

title: Outreach Strategy
quote: The most successful vending operators combine all three methods. Start in-person, follow up by phone, confirm by email.
description: How to secure your first location. The most effective approach is in-person visits — you build instant trust, stand out from the flood of emails and cold calls, and demonstrate real commitment to the partnership.

tasks.text: Identify your top 10 target locations within 20 minutes of your home.
Prepare a professional service proposal and marketing packet.
Execute in-person visits to your top 5 locations this week.
Follow up by phone to confirm the decision-maker's name, title, and availability.
Send professional email follow-ups with your service proposal and terms.
Secure at least one signed placement agreement.

tips: In-person visits are the most effective method: you build instant trust, stand out from cold calls, and can read body language in real time.
Walk into every meeting with a complete, professional packet. Location owners see a serious operator, not someone figuring it out.
Faster decisions; fewer follow-ups; more signed agreements — that is the result of professional presentation.

title: Building Systems
quote: Track every metric from day one. Operators who know their numbers scale faster.
description: Once you secure a location, the real business begins. Systems are what separate operators who scale from those who stay stuck at one machine. Build your profit tracking and inventory management systems from day one.

tasks.text: Set up a profit tracking spreadsheet: revenue, COGS, commissions, and net profit per machine.
Track your top 5 best sellers weekly and never let them run out.
Set a consistent restock schedule your location can rely on.
Remove and replace slow movers fast — dead stock is wasted shelf space.
Minimize waste: track expiry dates and rotate stock front-to-back.
Test new products in slow-mover slots for 2–3 restocks before making a final call.

tips: Snaxology operators benefit from AI-powered inventory tracking built into every smart cooler — real-time data, zero manual counting, and instant restocking alerts.
Revenue is not profit. Track Gross Sales, Cost of Goods Sold (COGS), and Operating Expenses separately for every machine.
Once you hit consistent profit, reinvest into your second machine. Treat every dollar of net profit as fuel for expansion.

title: Build Long-Term Growth
quote: Stop chasing locations. Start attracting them.
description: The operators who scale fastest treat their first machine like a proof of concept — they document everything, optimize relentlessly, and use that track record to open every door that follows. Build your digital foundation and scale your operation.

tasks.text: Buy a professional domain name and build a vending-specific website.
Set up a Google Business Profile for local search visibility.
Use your first location as a proof-of-concept and case study.
Reinvest profits strategically into your second and third machine.
Build referral relationships with location managers for warm introductions.
Document your process so every new location runs the same way.

tips: Snaxology handles the technology, the branding, and the service infrastructure — so you can focus on securing locations and growing your portfolio. Zero cost to the location. Fully managed. AI-powered.
With a strong website, locations begin reaching out to you. SEO-optimized structure drives inbound location leads 24/7.
Track performance by location to identify your highest-ROI sites and double down on what works.
